utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everybody in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Appearances for today. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Aditya Menon, and our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my colleagues in the courtroom. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. Nicholas Robson, I represent General Delic. Together with us are our legal assistants, Lana Deljkic and Asja Zujo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam. Can I just warn the witness first? Witness, good morning to you, too. Do you feel better today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I feel better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be aware of it, but I must warn you, as it is my duty, that you are bound still by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Okay? Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Yesterday we discussed some documents of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and I would like us to continue today. I will be clarifying some concepts later on. I believe that the witness might assist us here, some concepts that we discussed yesterday. I would like to show --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please look at D47. Thank you. Could we perhaps move the document slightly to the left. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The date on this document is the 23rd of December, 1993. Witness, let me read just a very small excerpt from this document that relates to criminal activities of Sabahet Isakovic, and it says in this document: "Today, on the 16th of July, 1993, according to the information from several sources, he probably hid the gun belonging to a foreign citizen who had attempted to assassinate Emir Mahmut Efendija Karalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm reading from the beginning of the 2nd paragraph in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you, first of all, do you know the Sabahet Isakovic? Have you heard of this person at all?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document tells us that a foreign national tried to assassinate Emir Mahmut Efendija Karalic. Did you know about this incident? Have you heard about it at all?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about an incident in which two foreign nationals allegedly tried to assassinate Karalic, and both were killed by the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like this document to be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 123.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Vidovic, I'm unsure about the meaning of this document. What is it you wish to prove or what information do you wish the Chamber to elicit from this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday we discussed the relations between the foreigners and the 7th Muslim Brigade. The indictment considers foreign fighters as members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and I want the witness to comment on the actual relations between the troops of the 7th Muslim Brigade and the foreign fighters. This document, in my belief, speaks to it, when taken with the other documents that we have exhibited and ones that we intend to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This seems, on the face of it, to be a document belonging to the investigation against a Sabahet Isakovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Isakovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. And in the course of this investigation, the attempted assassination of Emir Mahmut Efendija Karalic is mentioned, and it is mentioned in relation to the attempt being carried out by a foreign citizen. Now, that may very well be one of the Arabs, if we should call it this, I suspect this is what you have in mind, but it doesn't say so. This is a foreign citizen. It could be anyone. So how do you relate this document to the relationship between the Arabs and the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document says that Sabahet Isakovic hid the gun, and that is why the gun that was used in this assassination attempt. And that is why I asked the witness whether he knew about this incident, and the witness said, "I do. Two Arabs tried to kill Efendija Mahmut Karalic."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right, Witness, did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is why I showed this to the witness, precisely, because I wanted to clarify this dilemma that you just presented to us, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And to clarify the situation further, Witness, let me ask you: You told us that this incident was widely known?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second. Deal with the question by the Judge before you go back to the witness, and let's get done with that. I don't know whether the Judge is satisfied with your answer, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Not quite, because I have understood thus far that, indeed, it could be Arabs who are involved in this. But the next thing I read in the document is that this is an attempted murder or assassination that has to do with some money that one borrowed from the other and the selling of a gun and something else, and that doesn't seem to me to be of any particular interest, other than this is petty crime. It doesn't speak to any differences between the suspects and Mr. Karalic that would clarify the situation on political or religious grounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I explain? That is why it is sometimes a bad idea to read just small parts of the document. Let me read this: "According to the information from several sources, on 16th of July, 1993, he probably hid the gun belonging to the foreign citizen who had attempted to assassinate the Emir Mahmut Efendija Karalic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We have read the document --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I beg you for your indulgence. I have to read the sentence that follows, because otherwise I can't explain to you what this document is all about. Could I ask you for your permission to read the next sentence. "In the meantime, he borrowed 750 DM from the brigade, which he has not paid back to this day." So, on the one hand, this document says that on the 16th of July, he hid the pistol that was involved in this attempted assassination, and he also borrowed 750 DM from the brigade. These are two acts that are discussed in this document, the way I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And my question to the witness that relates to the assassination attempt on Mahmut Efendija Karalic is:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about the foreign nationals attempting to kill Mahmut, "Efendi," Karalic? And when I say "foreign nationals," I mean specifically Arabs. Did they try to assassinate him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you don't, in the process of answering a question from the Bench, go back to the witness. Deal with the Judge, finish with the Judge, and let the Judge satisfy himself that you have answered to his satisfaction, and then you can go to the witness. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I apologise, because I don't want to bring trouble to you, but I thought that what you wanted to prove here was a problematic relationship between the Arabs and the 7th Muslim Brigade, and perhaps some of the other members of the El Mujahedin, and those differences would be based on political, religious, moral grounds. And if that were the point, I would understand you, because that would be in your interest to show that there were severe religious and political and moral differences between these groups. Now, what you bring to me here is, to me, something that looks as simple petty crime. That would not, in my mind, bring much testimony to those religious differences, and that is why I asked about what is the meaning of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I thought that this document spoke to the relation between Arabs and the 7th Brigade, but I will withdraw this document, Your Honour, and I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would need some other clarification with regard to this whole episode that this document refers to, and, of course, in relation to your cross-examination, Mrs. Vidovic. Witness, I would like you to clear up something for us. You said yesterday, I believe, during the cross-examination, that the military police had no control over your units because general disorder and chaos reigned at the time. So with regard to this episode that you seem to be somewhat familiar with, at least, the military police -- was the police active, in fact, despite what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About this incident that did happen, Mahmut Efendija Karalic had his bodyguards. They were members of the military police. They were there to guard him. His security detail, they were with him. The two Arabs, one or two, tried to kill the efendi, and the police killed two Arabs protecting the efendi. So the police, actually they guarded Efendija Karalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And just one other thing. If I understand your answer correctly, the military police, rather than really controlling the situation and ensuring order in general, and the protection of all citizens, was ensuring the protection of certain particular individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the military police, part of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and Karalic had fears for his safety. And for that reason, he had to have guards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, if it was possible to have bodyguards for the protection of particular individuals, would you say that it was also possible to guarantee public order and, therefore, also the possibility to carry out investigations, to punish the behaviour of members of the military detachments, for example?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mahmut Efendija Karalic was the emir of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and he was entitled to this exclusive right to protection. And as for establishing order in other ways, the situation was not good. There were not enough forces to establish order. But he was the emir of the brigade, and he had this privilege.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, we've got to decide the fate of this document before you proceed. You have read extensively from it, virtually everything. Do you still need it admitted into evidence, when you have read it all into the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at this time, I will be withdrawing this document, and I will find some other way. Perhaps I could call the author of this document and have him explain about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now go back to some issues -- small issues that we were discussing yesterday, and I would like to ask you to clarify those issues so that the Chamber gets a clearer picture of some of the terms that we have been using here. In your evidence yesterday, you said that the Mujahedin were fighters on Allah's path; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some people call these men "Mujahids" and some call them "Mujahedin"; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it is one and the same category of people; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This term was used by the people to designate foreign fighters, but also the locals who had joined them; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All the foreign fighters, the Mujahedin, were not of African or Asian background; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Among them, there were Muslims from Europe, Turks, who looked more or less the same as the Bosnian fighters; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Members of the 7th Muslim Brigade often wore beards, and sometimes they dressed like the foreign fighters as Mujahedin in the field; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were many members of the 7th Muslim Brigade who wore long beards. There were quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that members of the 7th Brigade were often mistaken for foreign fighters because of the way they looked?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Even the members of other units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina who didn't know them personally would mistake them in this manner; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they looked the same. I can't -- well, yeah, that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in 1992 and 1993, you lived in Central Bosnia. It is true, is it not, that the Croatian media, radio/TV, would confuse the Muslimanske Snage, the 7th Muslim Brigade, the Mujahedin, and they would use the term "Muslimanske Snage," "Muslim Forces," to designate all of those?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I was captured by the HVO, I know that they used different terms for all -- all of them: MOS, Muslimanske Snage, the Mujahedin. They used those terms generally.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They considered -- or rather, let me rephrase the question. The BH Army was identified both with Muslimanske Snage and the Mujahedin; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they called all of us "the Mujahedin." They called us "Turks." They used all kinds of names. When I was captured, I heard from some HVO members who were in prison for some other offences, I heard what they were talking about, about what happened on the lines, that the Mujahedin were attacking from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "all of us," do you refer to the Muslim population or the Muslim fighters?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire BH Army. They called us "the Mujahedin," "the Turks," or some other names also.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your evidence yesterday, you said - and you confirmed several times - that in Central Bosnia there was chaos. And I would now like to show you a document that I believe to be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown D40.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you look at this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the record, I would like to say that this is a document originating from the 7th Muslim Brigade, dated the 30th of May, 1993, and the heading is "Reply to the 3rd Corps Command's Order" of the 27th of May, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me, ma'am. Did you say this document is dated the 30th of May? That's what the transcript says.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. That's what I said. I don't know what's recorded. The 30th of May, yes. Yes. Let me just clear this up to avoid any confusion. We have a stamp here that bears the date of the 30th of May, and then the title is "Reply to the 3rd Corps Command's Order," dated the 27th of May 1993. So we have two different dates. Was that the thrust of your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. My understanding of that document and those two dates is that the document is dated the 27th of May and not the 30th, but it was received by the 7th Mountain Brigade on the 30th, hence the stamp. That's the stamp for date of receipt, I would imagine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But the date of the document is the 27th, coming from whoever it comes from.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The document quite clearly shows that this is a reference. It is a reply to an order that was issued by the Corps Command on the 27th of May, 1993; and since it is signed by Asim Koricic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It really assists us when we can clarify things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let me quote. This is a very brief document, and I will say what it says here: "We are unable to obey Item 6 of your order, strictly confidential number 02/33-1281, of the 27th of May, 1993, because we do not have the insignia showing or belonging to the unit. We did not get these and so the process of marking has not even begun. I am addressing this letter to you in order to prevent unnecessary occurrences during the inspection of V/O, who are members of this unit, and to request that this unit be given the prescribed insignia." And before I move on to my question, I want to just ask you one thing. "V/O" can refer to the term of military conscripts; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document that bears the date on the stamp the 30th of May, 1993. On the face of it, we could conclude that on that date, the 7th Muslim Brigade did not have the proper insignia on that date. You were there at the time. You worked there at the time. It is true, is it not, that you did not have the insignia at that time?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 7th Brigade insignia came in only later. At that time, we wore all kinds of insignia, some of Muslimanske Snage, and some people didn't have any insignia at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, this document contains information that is accurate?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me now ask you another question. In our language, we call -- we use the term "amblemi" that indicate insignia of membership of a unit.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They are worn visibly attached to the sleeve of the uniform?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like this document to be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, has this document been given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Not yet, because we are, before we will admit it, discussing the probative value of the document. And I have, again, some reservations, because I'm not sure of exactly what it is you wish to prove with this document. I would imagine that your point of wishing to admit it is that it shows that there was no order, no system, in the 7th Muslim Brigade. They were running around, all of them, with either different or no insignia at all, and that you wish the Chamber to extract the information from this document that here you can see or here we can see that it was all a mess. I would be willing to go along with it, but the fact that for some time there were not enough insignia to put on everybody's uniform is, to me, not necessarily a sign of disorder. That could happen to, I guess, most military forces during an armed conflict. But I would ask you really to explain to us why you are admitting this -- seeking to admit this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to prove that on the 30th of May, 1992 [as interpreted], the process of putting insignia showing belonging to the 7th Muslim Brigade had not even started. This is highly relevant in these criminal proceedings because there will be witnesses testifying about the participation of men in battles, and it is very relevant to establish whether they were wearing insignia or not. I think this document shows clearly that they did not receive their insignia and that this process had not even started. Your Honours, I understood that, at this point, the admissibility of documents is being evaluated; whereas, the probative value will be assessed as part of the whole collection of exhibits and testimonies. I feel that this document is highly relevant because it shows that on the 30th of May, several days before the event in Maline, the process of putting insignia on the men of the 7th Muslim Brigade had not even begun; whereas, it is members of that brigade who are suspected of having committed these crimes. Have I been sufficiently clear for Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You have indeed, and your explanation now makes all the difference to me. I'm very happy now, because now I understand what it is you want. And I would like you, in the future - and also the Prosecution - to explain to us what you wish to prove here, because otherwise the Chamber is left in the dark. You may have understood it all because you have a plan for your Defence, but you need to show it to us and help and assist the Chamber. I would be in favour of admitting it, but let me consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mine is a procedural problem, ma'am, and I know we have not yet adopted the guidelines on presentation of evidence, but the point I'm going to raise has not been even commented upon by the parties, because I think I assume they accept the point; namely, that where you have read extensively from a document, it just burdens the record to even go ahead and admit the document again. Now, this is a very short document and you read it in its entirety. Do you still need the document to go in? The contents of the document are already on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is necessary. This document consists of two sentences, literally two sentences. I think that at the end of the trial, the transcript will be much clearer, as will the exhibits, if certain relevant parts of documents are in the transcript. I will not be doing this with long documents, Your Honours. We will be using documents of 200 pages or so. I will be quoting small extracts and seeking to admit only those, or rather, to have only those in the transcript. But this is a very short document, which is why I quoted it. Your Honours, if I do not quote the document, it is very hard to understand what we are talking about here. Your Honours, I will be very happy to explain the purpose every time, but this will lengthen the proceedings, and it will prolong the time of cross-examination, which is why I don't go into explanations of documents. So I'm seeking instructions from Your Honours. If I have to explain every time, of course, I will try to explain the purpose of each document, but -- I see my learned friend is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution expresses its support for the idea that Judge Harhoff has explained, but, again, I think I also share some concerns that my learned colleague from the Defence has with respect to the amount of time that might be required for some of the documents. We also have a bit of a concern about the procedure of explaining the relevance or probative value of documents in the presence of witnesses as these issues arise. And, of course, in order to excuse the witness, again, eats up additional time, which is, of course, a very precious commodity. I'm not sure how we can get out of this dilemma. I do understand the need for the Judges to understand precisely what the relevance and probative value of the documents are. And in that respect, I do reiterate what the Prosecution has said previously, that in 7(3) cases, particularly this case, it's primarily a circumstantial case. And a large number of documents that might at first glance -- which are both Prosecution and Defence documents, may not at first glance appear to be probative or to have a high degree of relevance, may through later witnesses or through later documentary evidence gain in probative value and relevance as all the evidence comes in. The only other point I would simply make is that I believe on page 15, line 5, there's an error in the transcript where at least the English version, Mrs. Vidovic refers to the date of the document on the screen as being 30 May 1992, and perhaps that's either a translation error or perhaps she misspoke. Of course, this document is 30 May 1993. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. I thought that the issue that Judge Harhoff had raised had been resolved, that we were now dealing with the issue that I was raising, and you didn't comment on what I said. Now, let me say this to you, then, Madam Vidovic. We will now admit this document, but can I ask you, please, in the future, if a document is this short, you can ask the witness to look at it. We can look at it ourselves, read it, and then put your questions. Don't read the document and then ask the document to be put into evidence when it is so short. I can understand if it is a long document, that are you going to focus the witness's attention to a specific part and you want to quote that part. That I understand. So do you think that guideline would help? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit 123.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The previous document was withdrawn and struck from the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. 123. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness now be shown document D41. And for the record, until the document appears on the screen, this is a document issued by the Command of the 3rd Corps, the Security Sector, and it is dated the 12th of September, 1993. Your Honours, the copy was very bad, which is why we ask -- we ask for you to see the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I think you have the document before you, and I will ask you to read the document, in view of Their Honours' instructions. The document shows that information was obtained that certain persons were using their military booklets as identification documents, and there's evidence of engagement in certain tasks. And the most frequent cause of this problem is the irresponsibility of certain organs, and that there is information that fictitious documents were being issued without the proper basis. Is that what the document says, Witness?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I won't quote from the document any further, but please try to go back in your mind to the year 1993, because I want to ask you questions about facts following from this document. While you were a member of the 7th Muslim, is it correct that people in the field used these military booklets to sell on the black market?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Did you say to sell the booklets on the black market?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that there were certain abuses of military booklets. I know that some people sold their military booklets. Everybody had to be mobilised. People who did not want to go to the front lines, to the defence lines, and who didn't want to join any unit tried in every possible way to obtain these booklets. I was near Travnik, and these were people from the town of Travnik, the ones that I knew of.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the purpose of buying such booklets was to have a booklet to show if there were any checks?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Either by the military police or the civil police; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You read this document?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does it reflect the actual situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it was like.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 124.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll move on to another topic. Witness, yesterday, you told us that, at a certain point in time, you joined a group of Arabs, and now I want to ask you the following: In mid-August 1993, approximately, you learned that there had been an agreement between the detachment and the army that it was to enter into the army establishment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I want to ask you the following in connection with this: It's correct, is it not, that groups of Arabs from Mehurici and Poljanice entered the detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's also correct, is it not, that El Mujahedin was made up of these groups?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it's also correct, is it not, that in a certain area of Central Bosnia, which was not very large, there were several groups of Arabs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For example, the Turkish group in Arnauti?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, excuse me. I don't know where the Turkish group was, but in the areas of Travnik and Zenica I know there were quite a few groups. But I can't tell you where each one was located exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Have you heard of the group at Bistricak?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Zeljezno Polje?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's correct, is it not, that these groups had nothing in common with El Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. These were separate groups. I don't know whether they had any contact at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of whether these groups acted independently or whether they were under someone's control?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, these were independent groups. They would join in some actions, but for the most part they were completely independent in their activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I'll go back to the detachment. The detachment had its emir? You said that more than once.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell Their Honours, if you know, what a shura is?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A shura is a kind of religious council or body which made decisions on certain matters. They could decide what should be done by a unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say" religious body," and when you say that they could make decisions as to what a unit could do, could you please clarify this for Their Honours? Would I be correct in saying that the shura was the supreme commanding body?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, it was the supreme commanding body?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was based on a religious foundation?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were probably not present at meetings of the shura, but you would know the following: The decisions of the shura were binding on members of the detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in your testimony, you described participating in some battles together with the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in reaching the following conclusion: Regardless of the fact that the detachment had been established as a unit of the army, it's true that its shura and emir continued making decisions as to whether the detachment would go into action or not?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The army could only discuss cooperation with the shura; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know any details about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding the activities of the detachment, it was the emir and the shura who decided. You told us that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: People did not go into certain battles if the shura said "No"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, for example, that the detachment did not go to fight around Buhine Kuce? Have you heard about that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the area correctly, but I know there were such instances.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It would be fair to say, would it not, that assessments of the situation were made in the detachment as to whether to go into action or not?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now put a proposition to you. If the shura decided that the detachment should not go into a certain battle with the army - and you said there was such cases - not even the late President Izetbegovic could have issued a different order; am I correct in assuming that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was the shura that issued these decisions. I can't go into details, but it's certain that the shura could decide differently. But I'm not aware of the details. The shura, if they felt the detachment should not go, they could make that decision. They could make a different decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When testifying about the participation of the El Mujahedin Detachment at Kruscica, in fighting with the army, you said that you knew that El Mujahedin participated in the fighting. But I want to suggest to you the following: It's correct, is it not, that at that time, during the fighting at Kruscica, there was a very serious incident, almost a clash, between the El Mujahedin Detachment and the armija, the army. And I will ask you the following: Before your arrest, a fighter of the Krajiska Brigade was arrested for being drunk by members of the detachment; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that situation very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness be shown document D37 in connection with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when the document shows up on your monitor, please read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could the usher zoom in, please, and show the document in its entirety. This document is entitled -- or rather, it's a document of the Glorious 17th Krajina Mountain Brigade, and it's dated the 25th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday that the Glorious 17th was at Kruscica, I think.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is. But if I can clarify, I heard about the situation from members of the detachment. I didn't see it myself, so I don't know precisely what happened, but they explained to me what happened after some time. I don't know exactly how much time had elapsed, and then I will say something about it later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So I understand that you know about the capture of a fighter. It says here of the Mixed Artillery Division of the Glorious 17th, Amir --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- Kuduzovic?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the document, if you've read it, it says that the army endeavoured to get its fighter back and to have him released, but quite simply they were rejected quite roughly, and they were made to leave the El Mujahedin camp in quite a rude manner. So I will ask you the following: You are not surprised, are you, by this attitude of the detachment towards the members of the armija who came to fetch their fighter who had been arrested by the El Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not surprised because the Arabs were very upset by the fact that the man had been drinking alcohol. They had methods of their own. There were other incidents, also, besides this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So this BH Army soldier was arrested solely because he had been intoxicated?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The man came there. He was not in the best of states, and he asked for some alcohol; and then they took him in purportedly to give him some alcohol.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that this soldier was not released when the BH Army intervened, but only when Mufti Abdibegovic intervened and the incident died down after that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 125.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will go back to the detachment itself. The Prosecutor showed you some photographs, and you were able to identify some members of the detachment. I would like to ask you, you knew Imad Al Mesri; did you not?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Judges who he was, what his role was in the detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was also some kind of a religious representative. He ran the religious school. He was some kind of a religious leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A religious leader. So we're talking about Imad Al Mesri, to make the transcript quite clear. You were at his lectures?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that he considered Corps members to be infidels and enemies of the faith?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, now I would like to show document D92 to the witness. It is an excerpt from a book by Evan Kohlmann, pages 118 and 119 in the English. That would be page 54 [as interpreted] In the B/C/S translation. I will be quoting from just a little excerpt from this book.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Page 154 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could just zoom in a little bit. The part is important for me. Could you please look at this document while we're waiting for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at this part where it says: "Among the textbooks used in this school was an essay ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have the English version. Okay. Thank you very much. This is the last paragraph in the English version at the very bottom of this page, Your Honours, the one that I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you have read this part, Witness, it says here that Imad Al Mesri, also known as Amad el-Masri. It says here that he was known for his regular instructions and lectures on the Islam. The book that was distributed by the Kuwaitis condemned the kuffar, the infidels, and their various attempts at self-government. You told us something about Imad Al Mesri. You said that he was a religious leader. Does this reflect what you actually told us?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So Imad Al Mesri criticised the infidels?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Judges, to your knowledge, how long was Imad Al Mesri in the detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was there until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I would like this document to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It will be admitted into evidence. May it be given an exhibit number? Just this page, Madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour, just this page, and its translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 118 of the translation. I don't know what the page number is on the -- 154 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the -- we have two pages in English and one page in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While I'm speaking, may I ask that when the witness is speaking, could we please switch off our mics, because otherwise it affects the voice distortion. So you'll have to ask questions, then switch on and off. Thank you very much. I know you've been doing that, but at times we forget. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We apologise. Now I would like the witness to be shown document D29.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt. The previous exhibit, the Exhibit number will be 126.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. 126.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Your Honour, I ask that the witness be shown document D29. And for the record, this is a document from the Command of the 3rd Corps in Zenica, the Security Sector, dated the 28th of November, 1993, that is entitled "Report on the Activities of Foreigners from Arab Countries in the Area of Responsibility of the 3rd Corps."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a long document, and I will be quoting just a very brief portion, in light of the length of this document. I will be quoting from the first paragraph, part of the first paragraph, where it says: "In contact with a colleague during the preparation in these days, we came by photocopies of letters addressed to Saudi Arabia, to Ebu Ahmed and Ebu D'Asira. In this letter sent to Saudi Arabia, a certain Imad, a fighter of the El Mujahedin Unit, informs Ebu Ahmed and Ebu D'Asira about the situation in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and states: 'I inform you that a difficult phase has started for us because there are many enemies, Communists. However, this phase represents a new phase of improvement in the road we follow. We are now one detachment. We have our own body, which is formally under the control of the army, but it cannot order us to engage in actions against our will. To the contrary, we set plans for them because they have little experience.'" Now, Witness, I want to ask you something about this. You told us that you knew a person by the name of Imad in the El Mujahedin Unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you agreed that he considered Communists the enemies of the faith; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in order for the Trial Chamber to understand what it is that we're talking about, it is true, is it not, that both the Arabs and the Muslims close to the religious circles considered former JNA officers to be Communists?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They also considered many of the politicians in Bosnia and Herzegovina to be Communists, the official authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, having heard this short quote, that Imad, in this letter, paints an accurate picture of the relationship between the El Mujahedin Unit and the army when he says: "We are now one detachment. We have our own body, which is formally under the army, but the army cannot order us to engage in actions against our will." Does this reflect the actual relations in the field?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify this a little bit. The Arabs, in fact, ran the detachment. We Bosniaks were not so well represented in this cadre. They could make decisions, and I can't say some things with certainty, but, yes, that's what they did. So they could decide otherwise, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, am I right, did I understand you correctly that you consider that this document reflects the accurate information?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could I get an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 127.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be asking you only two or three questions before our break.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that the detachment, throughout its existence, refused to wear the BH Army insignia? What I mean, I refer to the fleur-de-lys symbol.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Command Staff and the Arabs, they didn't want to wear them, but some Bosniaks who had perhaps brought them over from their original units, they may have worn them. But they were not generally worn.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The record says that "they were not generally worn," but what you actually said is they were not worn officially?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. They were not worn. Some people may have -- I'm talking now about the Bosniaks, because Arabs did not wear any insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question. The detachment refused to fight under the Bosnia and Herzegovina flag, and it had the fleur-de-lys symbol on it?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no such flag in the barracks, and it was not carried into action.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you to look at a brief video. It is D3. Do you see this, Witness? Can you see it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right -- can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that the detachment fought under this flag in all its combat activities?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now stop with my questions, and I would just like to tender this video into evidence. We're only interested in this part where this flag is seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The clip from this video is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 128.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand that it is now time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is indeed. Court adjourned, and come back at quarter to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, yesterday, you had said you'd take the first session. How much longer are you going to be still?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe maybe 15 minutes, not more. Of course, I didn't expect this lengthy discussion about the documents, but I've done my best to cut down the number of questions. So no more than 15 minutes, I'm sure of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness Exhibit 109.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look at the page 1 of this document. It is a document from the Zenica Security Services Centre in Zenica, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ministry of Interior. It is sent to the Secretariat of the Interior. This document was shown to you by the Prosecutor yesterday, and I would just like to ask you to look at what is here in this document.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that this document refers to the rules on keeping the record, the registration and de-registration of place of residence of foreign citizens; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that it says here in this document that on the 11th of October, 1994, all the legal requirements have not been met?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would then conclude that on the 11th of October, 1994, the Secretariat of National Defence in Zenica did not have the relevant data about foreign nationals. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were in the detachment. You know that the foreign nationals did not want to provide their personal details to anyone, not even to you in the detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. None of us Bosniaks knew their real names. And as for the documents, they handed them over to an Arab man in the Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to conclude that this was Abu Isa, would I be correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was Abu Isa. I know him. All the documents were handed over to him, but we didn't know the real names and we didn't really have any contacts with either their documents or their real names.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, am I right when I say that Abu Isa is related to Sheikh Enver, whom you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Abu Isa's sister was the wife of the deceased Sheikh Enver.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will now be asking you some questions about Sheikh Enver.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document can be put away. This is a document that is already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I have a question. Before you ask your next question, Ms. Vidovic, I would like you to clarify a point for me, or rather, I would like to ask the witness to clarify this point. Sir, I am talking to you. You've said that no one amongst the Bosnians knew the names, the real names of these foreigners. You also said that these people gave their name to the command post in Arabic. Does this mean that the authorities, that the Command knew who they were, knew their real names, and knew that they were actually members of various units in which they were fighting? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may before the witness answers this question. It's either a problem with the record, the transcript, or perhaps I misunderstood what the witness said. The witness said that they gave their names to Abu Isa, not to the Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right, Witness?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They all gave their documents to Abu Isa.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Abu Isa, to your knowledge, did he give those documents to the Superior Command, let's say the BH Army Command? Do you have an knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I know that they concealed their identity. We didn't know their real names, and Abu Isa held all those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now go back to Sheikh Enver. It is true, is it not, that he was a missionary?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a religious leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He was an Egyptian?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that he came to Bosnia and Herzegovina from Italy?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he came from Italy.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it is true that he came to Bosnia and Herzegovina in late 1994, not before that; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late 1994 or early 1995. I'm not quite sure, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So late 1994 or early 1995?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it's possible that it's late 1994. I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. If someone were to say that he was a member of the detachment from May 1995 -- I do apologise. If someone were to claim --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I just want to correct my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to claim that he was a member of the detachment from May 1993, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He showed up in late 1994. I don't think that he was there before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So until that time, from the time when you joined the detachment until the end of 1994, he did not show up in the detachment; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to ask you just a few more questions. Yesterday, you told us that several different groups had been operating in Bosnia-Herzegovina - I mean, groups of Arabs - in 1995 as well?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Abu Zubeir [Realtime transcript read in error "Zubaida"] Group, does that name mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard about Abu Zubeir, and I knew that he had a group.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Abu Zubeir?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Abu Zubeir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I want to make one thing clear, I'm talking about "Abu Zubeir," not "Abu Zubaida." These are two different persons. Witness, the Abu Zubeir Group, am I correct when I think that this group had -- was not on friendly terms with the El Mujahedin Detachment at all?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some problems, yes. They were separate. He was independent, and I know that they didn't come to the detachment at all. They may have even been prohibited from coming to the detachment, but I can't remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to show to the witness Exhibit 115. It's the personal records, Exhibit 115. And I believe, Your Honours, that this is a document under seal, so I don't know if we want to go into this document. I'm not going to be mentioning the witness's name. I just wanted to point out that this is a document that's been admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The HOS is the Croatian Defence Forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are different from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are different from the HVO, yes, Your Honour. They operated independently both of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were they a BiH unit? Did they exist only in Bosnia-Herzegovina or were they also there in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to the best of my knowledge, they existed both in Croatia and also in Bosnia-Herzegovina, or rather, some parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, especially in Herzegovina, but I think also in Central Bosnia and even in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm terribly sorry to interrupt, but I would like to ask a question. Actually, I'd like to put a question to the witness. Sir, you told us that this certificate, or rather, those certificates that were delivered to the Bosnians in the Bosnian Army, were also delivered to both forces, the HVO and the HOS. I would like to ask you if you know if those certificates were delivered to those two groups for the entire period of war, from 1992 to 1995 or end of 1995, or were those certificates only delivered to the Croatian forces during the first period while these forces fought against the Serbs, if I'm not mistaken, together alongside with the Bosnian Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know precisely. I think it was for the whole war from 1992 until 1995, but I'm not really familiar with that topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we will have an opportunity to clarify these issues with other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you about a person nicknamed Abu Ubeidah. You said that you knew him. Is it correct that this person was also called Ali Ahmet Ali Hamad?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know Abu Ubeidah very well. I'm not sure about this exactly, about Ali Ahmed, this other name. As he caused some problems after the war, I know about this. He caused the problem in Mostar, and I think that was his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of a person nicknamed Abu Aisa?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have done, but I don't remember who this man is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will go back to what you know. Abu Ubeidah, to the best of your knowledge, from August 1993 onwards, was he a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was never a member of the detachment. He had a group of his own first in the Karaula; and then later on in Bijelo Bucje, he had a group of his own.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'll ask you something. You're a local Muslim, are you not? Do you agree that the local Muslims were very sensitive in the Travnik area to the improper contacts between the Arabs and their young daughters who were under age?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember that they complained to Dr. Abu Haris while he was the emir, and that there was talk about this in the detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of several such incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether any such cases were ever linked to Abu Ubeidah?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Bijelo Bucje, there was an incident with an under-age girl. Something happened, I don't know exactly what. But I know that Abu Haris, who had authority and was educated, he was able to explain certain things. And he tried to draw Abu Ubeidah's attention to this, to give him advice, and even tried to issue an order to him, but Abu Ubeidah refused to listen to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understood you to say that he tried to prohibit such improper contacts with young girls to him.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because it damaged the reputation of all the Arabs. So he tried that, but Abu Ubeidah would not allow it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. While you were in Bijelo Bucje, the situation there was very difficult, was it not?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said yesterday, there were constant attacks by the Chetnik forces using tanks, artillery, infantry. So the situation was extremely difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I understood that there was a blockade by Serb and Croat forces. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were Serb forces on the one side in the direction of Donji Vakuf; and behind our back, there was some 15 Croatian villages. And for a long time, there was a total blockade, for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone were to say that at that time - and you were at Bijelo Bucje then - that they often went from Bijelo Bucje to Mehuric and back, that would not be possible, would it?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for a long time, nobody could move around. People had to stay where they were. Bijelo Bucje was the Bosniak village that was the furthest out, Bijelo Bucje and another village. And neither civilians nor soldiers nor anybody could move around for a long time:

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I have concluded my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution just has a few questions that arise out of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-2, I'd like to focus your attention on the period prior to the establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment. In that period prior to the unit being formally established, did the Arabs in Mehurici have a shura?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I can't say anything about that initial period, because I'm not really familiar with what went on then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me then ask you, PW-2, about the period after you joined the unit, the El Mujahedin Detachment. At any point in time, sir, did you ever attend any meetings of the Shura Council?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of the war, I was present once. They invited us Bosniaks, since it was towards the end of the war and they were supposed to leave; and, on one occasion, several of us Bosniaks were invited to attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, PW-2, to focus on the period the second half of 1993, when you first joined the El Mujahedin Detachment. During that time period, sir, can you tell us who the members of the Shura Council were?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very hard for me to say precisely, but Imad was certainly there, so was Abu Haris. I'm not sure who else. People at the top. There were Arabs. There were no Bosniaks there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-2, I'm going to ask you a question, and I want to stress the fact that I'm asking you about your personal knowledge and not whether you heard about this from anyone else, but whether you are personally aware of whether there were any meetings between the leaders of the El Mujahedin Detachment and the leaders or commanders of any unit of the ABiH 3rd Corps in 1993, when you were a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were in the Kruscica area, I know that Vahidin, "rahmetulali," had a contact with General Alagic. I know that for a fact. I don't know about any other contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, the transcript didn't catch the name. You said someone had a contact with General Alagic. Can you repeat the name of the person that you know had a contact with General Alagic?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vahidin, the late Vahidin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, PW-2, do you know who General Alagic was and what position he held at the time of this contact with Vahidin?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he was one of the commanders in the area. I'm not sure whether he was the corps commander at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say "one of the commanders in the area," commanding in which armed force?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a commander in the Army of BH, and I know that Vahidin had contacts with him. What sort of contacts these were and what happened, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, that this contact that you've described occurred when you were in the Kruscica area, can you give us an approximate time period that you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. It was August or September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-2, let me now turn to that part of your testimony when you told us about being on the front line with Arabs near Bijelo Bucje when you were part of the Muslimanske Snage. Do you know - and, again, I would ask you to limit your answer to what you know - do you know, if prior to the military operations along the front line at Bijelo Bucje, there were any meetings between the leadership of the Arabs and the leadership of the Muslimanske Snage?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know about any meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Earlier this morning, PW-2, you indicated in your testimony that the Shura Council could make ultimate decisions as to whether to join any combat operations. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know, PW-2, why the Shura Council retained flexibility in deciding whether or not to engage in military operations with other units of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not trust those units and the commanders of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. There was lack of confidence. Probably that is the reason. They just didn't trust them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know why?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's say yesterday, for example, we mentioned this action in Visoko in 1992. The Arabs thought that those officers had consciously pushed them into death. Well, they didn't respect the officers and the generals, and there may have been other reasons as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you elaborate, sir, on what you mean when you say "the Arabs thought that those officers consciously pushed them into death"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't explain it in detail. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-2, what type of missions was the El Mujahedin Detachment sent on or asked to perform?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this question does not arise from my cross-examination. The Prosecutor could have put this question before my cross-examination. I did not ask about the missions that the El Mujahedin Detachment was sent on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, without elaborating in any great detail in the presence of the witness, I believe this question relates to the last two or three questions I put to the witness, which does arise from the issue as to whether or not the Shura Council could make decisions about which operations to participate in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-2, let me ask you that question again. What type of missions was the El Mujahedin Detachment sent on or asked to perform during the period you were in that unit?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't know, but I do know that after the conflict with the Chetniks, conflicts arose with the Croats. The Bosniak villages were all blocked. They were all surrounded. They were all mixed up. There would be a Bosniak village, a Croat village, another Bosniak village. And I know that we participated in those actions to lift the siege, the block. For example, when we were at Kruscica, we were supposed to deblock the old part of Vitez Town, and we were simply supposed to link up our territories. We were afraid that in Stari Vitez, all the inhabitants might be killed, as had happened in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: PW-2, you were asked a few moments ago, or perhaps 45 minutes ago, about Abu Isa. Do you know, sir, if Abu Isa was a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for certain because I don't know, but he was there. He took some documents there. But whether he was there exactly, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, PW-2, when you say "he was there," what place are you referring to when you say "he was there"?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him on several occasions in the Vatrostalna barracks near Zenica, where we were stationed when we were on leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What function was the Vatrostalna barracks near Zenica being used for at this time?

utterances.speaker: PW-2 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was used as a barracks. The soldiers and the command were quartered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, sir, for the benefit of clarification, when you say "the soldiers and the command were quartered there," what soldiers and what command were in the Vatrostalna barracks near Zenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to object for the record. I did not cross-examine on the barracks in Zenica. I did not put a single question about this. Mr. Mundis could have put these questions during the examination-in-chief, and I want to say this for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness was asked questions about Abu Isa, and I'm simply trying to determine who this person was and where he was at the relevant time period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you asked the question, "What function was the Vatrostalna barracks near Zenica being used for at that time," is that still about Abu Isa?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can refer you to page 49, line 11, in response to a question, the witness said: "I saw him on several occasions in the Vatrostalna barracks near Zenica, where we were stationed when we were on leave." I'm simply asking him to clarify. He goes on to say: "It was used as a barracks. The soldiers and command were quartered there," on lines 15 and 16 of page 94. I'm simply asking him to clarify which soldiers and which command he was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection will then be overruled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
